comments.author: parksy333
comments.body_html: Hey, for making explosive ammo, the template property HasGrenaderComponent: true MUST be present, otherwise it does nothing. If editing/making a buckshot shell, then both ProjectileCount AND buckshotBullets must be present and at the same number, just when using a buckshot-type template. For slugs, as seen when looking at something like the 12/70 Dual Sabot round, only the ProjectileCount part seems to matter, as the buckshotBullets property is still set to 8, whilst ProjectileCount is set to 2. Additionally, if/when adding those properties in, if you could include Weight and PenetrationPowerDiviation properties, that would be amazing. The former is self-explanatory and the latter is a property that BSG uses to simulate rounds not always penetrating for whatever reason, as seen when shooting enemies with super-high pen rounds, and them somehow shrugging it off. A PenetrationPowerDiviation value of 1 means that the penetration capabilities can either go UP TO 100% higher or 100% lower, and this property is present on all projectiles in the game. Finally, for revolver-type weapons, each chamber is treated as its own magazine and the created projectile’s MongoID must be present in each of the cylinders’ accepted ammo ID lists. Unfortunately for the other properties, we cannot simply copy/paste them into the created ammo’s property list since (I believe) only your mod’s defined properties can be read and executed by the game, otherwise I probably wouldn’t be requesting this, haha.

comments.author: parksy333
comments.body_html: (sorry in advance for long post) - Hey, whenever you happen to have time to add that setting in, may I suggest adding the ammoHear and ammoDist properties in as well? The ammoHear property is exactly how it sounds and useful for creating subsonic ammo with suppressed bonuses when given negative values, whilst the ammoDist property stands for “Ammo Distribution” which adds penalties (maybe bonuses if negative value, needs more testing) for ballistic drops and shot groupings. Useful for creating variants of the base game’s homebrew ammo created by Mechanic, and provides an additional balancing option when creating extra-powerful ammo. Additionally, MinFragmentsCount and MaxFragmentsCount properties are missing, which are both a component of the already-present FragmentationChance, controlling how many frags are made when the bullet splits on impact, affecting total calculated damage. Finally, SpeedRetardation might be a useful additional property, which additionally fine-tunes a bullet’s per-meter speed/drop and damage drop-off rate. In core game files, it uses scientific notation for values - e.g. 2.3e-05 would represent 0.000023 per-meter speed drop-off. Basically, it’s how the game simulates air resistance/drag in addition to the other real-world ballistics simulations. The example value represents minimal drag, whereas if you look at shotgun pellets/slugs, the drag is drastically higher. Alright, that’s about it, sorry for the long post haha.
